label: q/a/e/w/o/c input at original positions 2-5, after context tokens like h, r, 2
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at positions t=2..6 (mostly t=3-4; never at t=0,1, the delimiter or copy phase). The current input is almost always one of q, a, e, w (about 78% of mass), then o, c, and weakly 0 or d; usually the first occurrence of that token. Activation depends strongly on which tokens came earlier: the strongest examples come after prefixes made of h, r, 2, l, p, k, 3, i, s, m (for example h 2 2 r [e], 2 r r r [q]). The q/a/e/w/o/c-at-t=2..5 condition by itself covers about 95% of mass but has only 17% precision. Requiring at least two of those context tokens before the step brings dev F1 to about 0.47 (mass recall 0.73). The rest of the prefix dependence is distributed, and I could not reduce it to a simple token set.
